Coupled Technique(s).cell: SF-ICP-MS — Ti on a Finnigan ELEMENT at PML (§2.1.2)

Coupling Description.cell: The Q-ICP-MS measures B, Zr, Nb, Mo, Sn, Sb, Hf and Ta, and its Nb (from Nb/Mo and Nb/Zr) is used for the SF-ICP-MS Ti calculation on the same solutions — §2.5, §2.8
Coupling Description.value: The Q-ICP-MS measures B, Zr, Nb, Mo, Sn, Sb, Hf and Ta, and its Nb (from Nb/Mo and Nb/Zr) is used for the SF-ICP-MS Ti calculation on the same solutions

Target Material.cell: basalt; andesite; peridotite; carbonaceous chondrite — GSJ and USGS RMs, and Ivuna, Orgueil, Cold Bokkeveld and Allende

Sampling Unit Type.cell: Weighed test portion -- "Approximately 20 mg of basalt and andesite samples were weighed"; "Approximately 50 mg for peridotites and approximately 10 mg for meteorites were weighed"; 9-18 mg for carbonaceous chondrites
Sampling Unit Type.value: Weighed test portion -- "Approximately 20 mg of basalt and andesite samples were weighed"; "Approximately 50 mg for peridotites and approximately 10 mg for meteorites were weighed"; 9-18 mg for carbonaceous chondrites

Sample Preparation Method.cell: Powders weighed with the B, Zr–Hf and Mo–Sn–Sb spikes and decomposed with 30 mol/l HF and mannitol, dried, dissolved in 0.5 mol/l HF, fluorides removed by centrifuging, and the supernatant diluted — §2.5; GSJ samples and PCC-1 further pulverised (§2.3)
Sample Preparation Method.value: Powders weighed with the B, Zr–Hf and Mo–Sn–Sb spikes and decomposed with 30 mol/l HF and mannitol, dried, dissolved in 0.5 mol/l HF, fluorides removed by centrifuging, and the supernatant diluted

Digestion Acid(s).cell: ultrasonic HF decomposition: 30 mol/l HF; bomb HF decomposition: 30 mol/l HF; re-dissolution: 0.5 mol/l HF — §2.5

Digestion Vessel Type.cell: Teflon (TFM-PTFE) bomb for peridotites and meteorites — §2.2.3, §2.5
Digestion Vessel Type.value: Teflon (TFM-PTFE) bomb for peridotites and meteorites

Digestion Step.cell: ultrasonic HF decomposition (basalts and andesites, <70 °C); bomb HF decomposition (peridotites and meteorites, 245 °C, mannitol added after heating); re-dissolution (dried, then 5 ml 0.5 mol/l HF in an ultrasonic bath, fluorides removed by centrifuging) — abstract; §2.5

Digestion Temperature.cell: ultrasonic HF decomposition: <70 °C; bomb HF decomposition: 245 °C; re-dissolution: N — abstract

Final Solution Matrix.cell: all: 0.5 mol/l HF with mannitol, diluted — 'The mannitol and HF concentrations in all samples and standard solutions were diluted to be similar to each other' (§2.5)

Chromatographic Separation Applied.cell: None — the method 'does not require ion-exchange separation' (§1); only the Zr–Hf spike was purified

Isotope Dilution Spike.cell: 10B spike; 91Zr–179Hf mixed spike; 97Mo–119Sn–121Sb mixed spike — §2.2.2–2.2.4; Nb and Ta are not spiked

Instrument Manufacturer.cell: Agilent -- "A Q-pole type ICP mass spectrometer, Agilent 7500 cs (Yokogawa Analytical Systems, Japan)"
Instrument Manufacturer.value: Agilent -- "A Q-pole type ICP mass spectrometer, Agilent 7500 cs (Yokogawa Analytical Systems, Japan)"

Torch Type.cell: Quartz glass torch with Pt injector — Table 1a
Torch Type.value: Quartz glass torch with Pt injector

Interface Cone Configuration.cell: 1 mm Pt sampler + 0.4 mm Pt skimmer (stated Table in section 2.1.1)
Interface Cone Configuration.value: 1 mm Pt sampler + 0.4 mm Pt skimmer (stated Table in section 2.1.1)

Sampler and Skimmer Cone Material.cell: Pt sampler and Pt skimmer (stated Table in section 2.1.1)
Sampler and Skimmer Cone Material.value: Pt sampler and Pt skimmer (stated Table in section 2.1.1)

Collision/Reaction Cell (CRC) Configurat.cell: all: no gas introduced into the octopole collision cell — 'collision gases were not introduced into the cell' (§2.1.1)

value.value: no gas introduced into the octopole collision cell

Detector Configuration.cell: Pulse counting and analog (>10^6 cps), switched automatically — Zr, Nb, Mo and Sb sometimes in analog at DF < ~250 (§2.1.1)
Detector Configuration.value: Pulse counting and analog (>10^6 cps), switched automatically

Nebulizer Type.cell: Micro-flow PFA nebulizer PFA-20 (ESI, USA); self-aspiration (stated Table in section 2.1.1)
Nebulizer Type.value: Micro-flow PFA nebulizer PFA-20 (ESI, USA); self-aspiration (stated Table in section 2.1.1)

Spray Chamber Type and Cooling Temperatu.cell: Scott double-pass, cooled at 2 °C, made of Teflon — Table 1a
Spray Chamber Type and Cooling Temperatu.value: Scott double-pass, cooled at 2 °C, made of Teflon

Sample Uptake Rate.cell: N — self-aspiration (Table 1a); pseudo-FI uses 0.013 ml per sample (§2.6)

Analytical Mode.cell: Flow injection -- "pseudo-FI" declared as the data acquisition mode; sec 2.6 "Pseudo-flow injection (FI) method for ICP-QMS", explicitly contrasted with "the continuous sample introduction method"
Analytical Mode.value: Flow injection -- "pseudo-FI" declared as the data acquisition mode; sec 2.6 "Pseudo-flow injection (FI) method for ICP-QMS", explicitly contrasted with "the continuous sample introduction method"

Target Species.cell: B, Zr, Nb, Mo, Sn, Sb, Hf, Ta — Ti is measured by the SF-ICP-MS

Reported Variables and Units.cell: B, Zr, Nb, Mo, Sn, Sb, Hf, Ta (µg/g) — Tables 5–8; Nb from Nb/Zr and Nb/Mo, Ta from Ta/Mo and Ta/Hf, and their averages

Monitored Masses.key: defines: monitored property per target species
Monitored Masses.cell: 10B, 11B → B; 90Zr, 91Zr → Zr; 93Nb → Nb; 95Mo, 97Mo → Mo; 118Sn, 119Sn → Sn; 121Sb, 123Sb → Sb; 178Hf, 179Hf → Hf; 181Ta → Ta — 'In one scan, 10B, 11B, 90Zr, ... and 181Ta were measured' (§2.1.1)

Number of Scans per Replicate.cell: all: 48 scans in 30 s, 1 point per mass — Table 1a

value.value: 48 scans in 30 s, 1 point per mass

Analysis Sequence.cell: Standard solution every two samples; each sample ~6 min including ~3 min wash. Pseudo-FI: a 40 s background step with the probe in the sample, then 30 s of sample signal — §2.1.1, §2.6
Analysis Sequence.value: Standard solution every two samples; each sample ~6 min including ~3 min wash. Pseudo-FI: a 40 s background step with the probe in the sample, then 30 s of sample signal

Wash Time Between Samples.cell: ~3 min with 0.5 mol/l HF — §2.1.1; background measured after a 200 s wash (Table 1a)

Internal Standard Element.cell: all: the ID-determined Zr, Mo and Hf, as references for Nb and Ta (ID-IS) — §2.8, §3.5; Mo is preferred

value.value: the ID-determined Zr, Mo and Hf, as references for Nb and Ta (ID-IS)

Drift Correction Method.cell: Mass discrimination from the standard solution average, usually without drift over 2 h; when drift was observed, the standard measured before and after the sample was averaged — §2.7, §2.8
Drift Correction Method.value: Mass discrimination from the standard solution average, usually without drift over 2 h; when drift was observed, the standard measured before and after the sample was averaged

Calibration Strategy per Target Species.cell: B, Zr, Mo, Sn, Sb, Hf: isotope dilution (Eq. 1); Nb, Ta: isotope dilution–internal standardisation (ID-IS) against Zr, Mo or Hf — §2.7, §2.8

value.value: isotope dilution–internal standardisation (ID-IS) against Zr, Mo or Hf

Blank / Background Correction Method.cell: Background measured before each sample after a 200 s wash, and procedural blank corrections from Table 4 applied to all analyses — Table 1a; §3.6, corrections usually <1% in basalts and andesites and <4% in peridotites and meteorites
Blank / Background Correction Method.value: Background measured before each sample after a 200 s wash, and procedural blank corrections from Table 4 applied to all analyses

Pulse/Analog Detector Nonlinearity Corre.cell: all: P/A factor determined each day before measurement — §2.1.1

value.value: P/A factor determined each day before measurement

Isotope Dilution Data Reduction Method.cell: Eq. 1 with the pseudo-concentration Q calibrated on spike–standard mixtures, and the mass discrimination correction factor applied to the measured ratios — §2.7
Isotope Dilution Data Reduction Method.value: Eq. 1 with the pseudo-concentration Q calibrated on spike–standard mixtures, and the mass discrimination correction factor applied to the measured ratios

Memory Effect Mitigation.cell: 0.5 mol/l HF as carrier and wash, which washes out Zr, Nb, Hf and Ta; ~20 min of 0.5 mol/l HF after REE work in HNO3 — §2.1.1
Memory Effect Mitigation.value: 0.5 mol/l HF as carrier and wash, which washes out Zr, Nb, Hf and Ta; ~20 min of 0.5 mol/l HF after REE work in HNO3

Uncertainty Level.cell: RSD% with observed ranges in parentheses
Uncertainty Level.value: RSD% with observed ranges in parentheses

Calibration Factor and Determination Met.cell: B, Zr, Mo, Sn, Sb, Hf: mass discrimination correction factor, natural ratio over the measured standard average (0.87–0.96 for 11B/10B, 0.94–1.04 for the others); Nb, Ta: relative concentration factor f_J against the reference element, from the standard solution — §2.7, §2.8

value.value: mass discrimination correction factor, natural ratio over the measured standard average (0.87–0.96 for 11B/10B, 0.94–1.04 for the others)
relative concentration factor f_J against the reference element, from the standard solution

Analysis Inclusion and Rejection Criteri.cell: Partially -- "Orgueil and Allende were analyzed 4 times and twice from the sample digestion, respectively. ... As the sample amounts used were small, and the carbonaceous chondrites are heterogeneous, analytical results for each run are shown in the table" alongside the averages. No acceptance or rejection rule stated
Analysis Inclusion and Rejection Criteri.value: Partially -- "Orgueil and Allende were analyzed 4 times and twice from the sample digestion, respectively. ... As the sample amounts used were small, and the carbonaceous chondrites are heterogeneous, analytical results for each run are shown in the table" alongside the averages. No acceptance or rejection rule stated

Combination Method.cell: all: average of repeat runs per sample — 'Orgueil and Allende were analyzed 4 times and twice from the sample digestion, respectively ... analytical results for each run are shown in the table' alongside the averages; bomb-method yields are the 'Average of two tests'

value.value: average of repeat runs per sample

Constants and Reference Values Used.cell: Spike ratios 91Zr/90Zr 29.0, 97Mo/95Mo 201, 119Sn/118Sn 30.1, 121Sb/123Sb 199, 179Hf/178Hf 25.1, against natural 0.218, 0.600, 0.355, 1.34, 0.499 (Rosman and Taylor 1998); 11B/10B spike 0.05348 and natural 4.053 by TIMS (Makishima et al. 1997) — §2.7
Constants and Reference Values Used.value: Spike ratios 91Zr/90Zr 29.0, 97Mo/95Mo 201, 119Sn/118Sn 30.1, 121Sb/123Sb 199, 179Hf/178Hf 25.1, against natural 0.218, 0.600, 0.355, 1.34, 0.499 (Rosman and Taylor 1998); 11B/10B spike 0.05348 and natural 4.053 by TIMS (Makishima et al. 1997)

Primary Calibration Standard Name.cell: all [B, Zr, Nb, Mo, Hf, Ta: mixed standard solution from the Alfa Aesar Specpure refractory metals plasma standard (Stock No. 44270); Sn, Sb: the same mixed solution, from Kanto Kagaku AAS solutions] — §2.2.6; isotope and element ratios checked against CLMS-4 (Spex)

value.value: mixed standard solution from the Alfa Aesar Specpure refractory metals plasma standard (Stock No. 44270)
the same mixed solution, from Kanto Kagaku AAS solutions

Secondary Reference Materials.cell: JB-1, JB-2, JB-3, JA-1, JA-2, JA-3, JP-1, BHVO-1, AGV-1, PCC-1, DTS-1 — §2.3; the chondrites are samples

Detection Limit Method.cell: all: 3σ, calculated for silicate samples at the dilution factor of ~340 where matrix effects are absent — §3.6

value.value: 3σ, calculated for silicate samples at the dilution factor of ~340 where matrix effects are absent

Counting Statistics Error.key: sample > sampling unit x reported property

Internal (Within-Measurement) Analytical.key: sample > sampling unit x reported property

Between-Session (Long-Term) Analytical P.cell: JB-1, JB-2, JB-3, JA-1, JA-2, JA-3, JP-1, BHVO-1, AGV-1, PCC-1, DTS-1 [all: average reproducibility 1.0–4.6% RSD] — §3.7, Tables 5–6; Mo in JB-1 (15%) excluded as heterogeneous

Analytical Accuracy and Assessment Metho.cell: JB-1, JB-2, JB-3, JA-1, JA-2, JA-3, JP-1, BHVO-1, AGV-1, PCC-1, DTS-1 [all: compared with reference values (Govindaraju 1994, Imai et al. 1995 and others)] — Tables 5–6; 'a significant difference exists for B in JA-2'

value.value: compared with reference values (Govindaraju 1994, Imai et al. 1995 and others)

Additional Notes.cell: Pseudo-flow injection with the ASX-100 autosampler; recovery yields from Ca–Al–Mg fluorides tested in 19 synthetic solutions (§2.4, §2.6)
Additional Notes.value: Pseudo-flow injection with the ASX-100 autosampler; recovery yields from Ca–Al–Mg fluorides tested in 19 synthetic solutions (§2.4, §2.6)
